sections.title: Formal equivalents
sections.content:
Choosing the right level of formality is crucial in advanced English:
• assist (formal) vs help (neutral). We are here to assist you with any enquiries.
• commence (formal) vs start/begin (neutral). The ceremony will commence at 10 a.m.
• reside (formal) vs live (neutral). She resides in the capital.
• terminate (formal) vs end (neutral). The contract was terminated due to a breach.
• endeavour (formal) vs try (neutral). We shall endeavour to resolve this promptly.

sections.title: Informal expressions
sections.content:
Informal language sounds natural in casual conversation:
• kids (informal) vs children (neutral). The kids are playing outside.
• loads of (informal) vs a great deal of (formal). There were loads of people at the party.
• grab (informal) vs obtain (formal). Let's grab a coffee after class.
• fed up with (informal) vs dissatisfied with (formal). I'm fed up with waiting in queues.
• figure out (informal) vs determine (formal). We need to figure out what went wrong.

exercises.question: Which is the FORMAL equivalent of 'start'?
exercises.explanation: Commence is the formal way to say 'start' or 'begin'.

exercises.question: Which is the INFORMAL way to say 'obtain'?
exercises.explanation: Grab is the informal equivalent of 'obtain' or 'get'.

exercises.question: 'Reside' is the formal equivalent of:
exercises.explanation: Reside is the formal way to say 'live' in a particular place.

exercises.question: Which INFORMAL phrase means 'dissatisfied with'?
exercises.hint: You're frustrated and tired of something.
exercises.explanation: Fed up with is the informal expression for being dissatisfied or annoyed.

exercises.question: The formal word for 'try' is:
exercises.hint: Very formal, used in business letters.
exercises.explanation: Endeavour is a very formal word meaning to try hard to achieve something.

exercises.question: 'Loads of' is the informal way of saying:
exercises.explanation: Loads of is informal for 'a large amount of' or 'a great deal of'.

exercises.question: Which formal word means 'end' a contract?
exercises.explanation: Terminate is the formal equivalent of 'end', especially for contracts.
